summary: A private white light, about 66 ft (20 m) tall, marking the entrance of the old Broadwater Beach hotel marina in Biloxi; the marina was destroyed by Katrina in 2005 but the light survived.

structures.note: Directory gives 1965 with a question mark. Tower has a gallery and an open lantern.

staffing.note: No keeper or caretaker named in the sources read.

access.note: Directory: site open, tower closed. The USLHS record says 'Open to Public: No', which disagrees with the directory. Johnston (2023) found the site in poor condition, with graffiti and a rusty pier railing.

facts.owner: Broadwater Development LLC (private, per the Lighthouse Directory)

events.note: Built for the Broadwater Beach Hotel/Resort marina. Directory gives 1965 with a question mark; the Lighthouse Hunters page also gives 1965 with a question mark; Flickr caption and Johnston give 1965.

Hurricane Camille. Johnston: light survived with minor damage while the resort was badly damaged. Lighthouse Hunters: the resort was destroyed; the page says nothing about the light in 1969. Not a direct conflict; no source gives a contemporary account of the light.
Hurricane Katrina (25 August 2005, per the Flickr caption) destroyed the hotel and marina; the light survived with minor damage. A March 2007 photograph shows it standing.

June 2020: Dakia Entertainment Hospitality and Broadwater Development, LLP signed a letter of intent to redevelop the hotel, marina and golf course as a $1.2 billion, 266-acre entertainment complex (WLOX). The directory's '$12 billion' appears to be a misprint.

corrections.why: A Mississippi light with an English name in every English source read (directory, Johnston, Flickr, Lighthouse Hunters). The French label appears to come from Wikidata/French Wikipedia; the guide keeps French names only for Quebec.
The directory gives USCG 4-9570, and the record's own source key is uscg_light_list:4-9570. The 4-9750 is probably a transposition.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Lighthouse Directory gives a $12 billion casino; WLOX reported a $1.2 billion, 266-acre complex in June 2020. The directory's figure is probably a misprint, and the story uses the WLOX figure.

notes_for_editor: (1) THIN-TO-MODERATE STATION. The sources are a directory, two personal accounts (Johnston's 2023 visit, the Flickr caption), a fan site, one news report, and a society record. (2) Not read: the Sun Herald reports from 2024-2025 (search snippets only). Those snippets say marina restoration work was under way and that a casino at the Broadwater might move ahead in 2025. The fetches timed out, so nothing from them is cited. The 'Today' section stops at the 2022 directory and the 2023 visit. An editor should check the current marina and casino status before publication. (3) Camille: Johnston reports that the light survived with minor damage; the Lighthouse Hunters page says the resort was destroyed in 1969 and says nothing about the light. These are not a direct conflict, and the story states only what each source says. (4) Build date: 1965, with a question mark on both the directory and the Lighthouse Hunters page; no primary source, no USCG or ARLHS date. The ARLHS register (USA-1240) was read only for its existence in the list since 2006; it is not cited. (5) Not used: an unsourced Facebook group post with a 1971 aerial photo of the hotel and light, which the story does not rely on. (6) Not verified: the USCG Light List entry (4-9570 versus 4-9750) and the characteristic, which come from the record and the directory (ENC/Light List not read). (7) Newspapers: Chronicling America was not searched. Its Mississippi coverage would not reach 1965 in any case. (8) Access: the directory says the site is open and the tower closed; the USLHS record says 'Open to Public: No'. The story states both. An editor should confirm the current access status before publication.
